nonClaims: THE REASON DOES NOT REACH THE SERVER ON THIS HEAD. commitGmCombatRewind serialises a fixed five-field body, so the `reason` this hook attaches to the commit argument is dropped before the POST, and POST /api/matches/[id]/rewind-commit still writes the module constant REWIND_COMMIT_REASON into the private record. The capture is real, the persistence is not, and neither file is in this unit's ownership.

E2E-25 IS NOT SATISFIED BY THIS UNIT. Its THEN clause - player views show the authorized result while only the GM private record contains the private detail - needs the server half. The row itself remains a later R6.umbrella row; this unit only unblocks it (units.json rowsUnblocked: [E2E-25]).

NO LADDER / PLAYWRIGHT RUN. The charter forbids both. e2e/gm-two-player-privacy.pack.spec.ts and e2e/networked-command-proof.spec.ts assert on the same test ids this unit moved between files; nothing here proves those specs still pass, only that the ids, the container and the two buttons are byte-identical in what they render for the callers that wired them before.

NO BUILD. next build was not run, so nothing here proves the lobby route compiles under the production compiler. tsc --noEmit passed on the full project, which is the type-level half of that claim and not the bundling half.
NO BROWSER EVIDENCE. Nobody clicked Preview GM Fix or Approve GM Fix against a live server; the producers are proven against injected doubles and the rendering against jsdom.

THE STATUS LINE IS NEW BEHAVIOUR, NOT A CHARTER DELIVERABLE. NetworkedHostGmControls now renders one authored sentence for whatever a promise-returning producer answers, so that the two buttons are not a control that calls the server and shows nothing (defect #15's shape). It is inert for a caller whose handlers return void, so the /e2e proof page's DOM is unchanged. Flagged for the reviewer as the one place the implementation went past the charter's literal deliverable list.

THE CORRECTION CONTROLS DO NOT OPEN THE BLAST-RADIUS DIALOG. That dialog belongs to NetworkedGmRewindControls, which mounts beside these controls on the same lobby surface and is wired to the same request by buildGmRewindRequest. The correction control shows the same preview's summary sentence inline instead of a second dialog.

NO CONCURRENCY GUARD BETWEEN THE TWO GM CONTROLS. The rewind confirm and the correction approve now both commit the same request from the same surface; nothing serialises them on the client. A double apply is refused by the server's correction lease, which is not exercised here.
